title: Indigenous Science & Education Resources
text:
This developing collection brings together publicly discoverable resources on Indigenous histories, education, science, and decolonization. It is intended as a starting point for educators, researchers, and community partners—not as a substitute for relationships with Indigenous communities or community-specific guidance.
Explore the resource library →


This is an early prototype built from a small working inventory. Resource descriptions, categories, permissions, and the site’s future direction are subject to review with the Indigenous scholars helping curate the collection.




California Native History: Regional histories and Indigenous perspectives.
Indigenous Education: Scholarship on science education and land-based learning.
Decolonization: Introductory talks and reflections.

Browse the full library or learn about stewardship and contributions.

California Native History · Video


Coast Miwok Culture, Past, Present and Future with Dean Hoaglin


Mill Valley Library · 2024


Join a discussion led by Coast Miwok Tribal Council President Dean Hoaglin on the re-opening of the Museum of the American Indian (MAI), the Land Back Movement, and how to practice allyship. Dean Hoaglin, MAI Board President, is a lineal descendant of the Tamal’ko Coast Miwok of the Huukuiko Band from the village of Etcha Tamal (Nicasio), with ancestral ties to Olumpali (Novato) and Liwanelowa (Sausalito), and was trained in traditional teachings and practices with family elders from a young age. For more than 25 years Dean has worked in social services promoting health, wellness and educational opportunities for local Native people in a culturally responsive manner.

California Native History · Podcast


Coming Home to the Cove: A Story of Family, Memory, and Stolen Land


Adam Loften, Emergence Magazine · 2022-2025


Across the United States, Indigenous communities are calling for sweeping revisions to stories commonly told as “history”—stories that, even today, neglect and erase Indigenous peoples and serve as justification for continued ownership of stolen Indigenous lands. This series is the multigenerational story of a Coast Miwok family’s eviction from their ancestral home in Northern California and one woman’s mission to bring the living history of her family back to the land. Throughout this series, Theresa Harlan chronicles the story of her family’s displacement from their homestead on a cove in Tomales Bay and shares her grassroots efforts to involve the wider community in protecting both the history and the future of this place. As she tells her family’s story, Theresa makes a powerful claim: remembering and retelling inclusive histories has the power to create a more just future. In this series we ask: Who gets to define history? In what ways is it our responsibility to ensure that a shared history is an accurate and just representation of the places we call home?

California Native History · Video


Why The Gold Rush Is One Of The Darkest Moments In US History


2021


Beneath the promise of gold in California in the late 1840s and early 1850s, white settlers were well armed and prepared to kill Native Americans who lived there. These violent attacks against Native Americans were often supported and funded by the state’s newly created government. To uncover more details about the gold rush, we spoke with Jayden Lim and Nicole Myers-Lim of the California Indian Museum and Benjamin Madley, author of "An American Genocide."

Decolonization · Video


Decolonization is for Everyone


Nikki Sanchez · 2019


“This history is not your fault, but it is absolutely your responsibility.” A history of colonization exists and persists all around us. Nikki discusses what colonization looks like and how it can be addressed through decolonization. An equitable and just future depends on the courage we show today. “Let’s make our grandchildren proud”. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community.

Decolonization · Video


How to decolonize Canada, starting with you


Kevin Lamoureux · 2022


Decolonization is a word that is often met with resistance. Too often discussions about decolonization lead to unnecessary fear or hostility. There is another possibility. Decolonization can be an invitation for all Canadians to be a part of something good and to leave behind a better version of Canada for generations to come. Kevin Lamoureux is a Faculty member at the University of Winnipeg and a well known public speaker. He has served as Associate Vice President for the University of Winnipeg, Education Lead for the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation, and as Scholar in Residence for several school divisions.
He is an award winning scholar with an impressive publication and research grant record, and has consulted for governments, organizations and institutions across Canada. His most recent book contribution, for Ensouling Our Schools with Dr. Jennifer Katz, is being used by educators across Canada working to create inclusive spaces for all students. He has been seen on TV, in documentaries, in print, and in the media. More than anything, Lamoureux is committed to reconciliation and contributing to an even better Canada for all children to grow up in. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community.

title: About & stewardship
text:
Attribution and permissions
The library links to source materials rather than redistributing copies. A publicly accessible link does not necessarily grant permission to reproduce, adapt, or teach from a resource in every context. Check the original source and relevant community protocols.

title: About & stewardship
text:
Proposed curation process

Suggest a resource and its original source link.
Confirm authorship, context, and whether public indexing is appropriate.
Review descriptions and topic labels with curators.
Publish, revise, or withdraw entries as appropriate.
